title: On divisor sums due to Erdős and Ramanujan
summary: Let $d(n)$ denote the number of divisors of a positive integer $n$. A classical problem in analytic number theory is given by the asymptotic behavior of the divisor sum $\sum_{n \leq x} \frac{1}{d(n)}$, with Ramanujan having introduced an asymptotic formula for this sum with an explicit evaluation for the constant $A_1$ for the leading term $A_1 \frac{x}{\sqrt{\log x}}$. Gabdullin et al. recently considered a hybrid of this problem and the Titchmarsh divisor problem concerning $\sum_{p\leq x} d(p-1)$, proving that $\sum_{p\leq x} \frac{1}{d(p-1)} \asymp \frac{x}{(\log x)^{3/2}}$.
